## Setup

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(simling)
```

`simling` is an R package of simulated linguistic data. If it is not installed yet, run these two lines once, in the Console:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mcanzi/simling")
```

## The data

In `dgs_iconicity`, 30 deaf signers of German Sign Language (DGS) and 30 hearing people who do not sign rate 300 DGS signs for **iconicity**: how much a sign looks like what it means, from 1 (not at all) to 7 (very much). Deaf signers also rated each sign's age of acquisition (`aoa`, in years). The code below makes one row per sign, with the mean rating of each group:

```{r}
signs <- dgs_iconicity |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating), .by = c(sign, aoa, group)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = rating) |>
  rename(signers = `deaf signer`, non_signers = `hearing non-signer`)
glimpse(signs)
```

Today's question: are iconic signs learned earlier, and which group's ratings tell us more about it?
